instruction: Empty all liquids, lightly rinse, and place in the blue recycling bin. Keep caps on or off according to local municipal sorting rules.
preparationSteps: 1. Empty liquids • 2. Quick cold rinse • 3. Crush to save space
upcyclingIdea: Cut horizontally to build a self-watering herb planter or DIY drip irrigation bottle.

instruction: Rigid plastic tubs (yogurt, takeout, margarine) marked #1, #2, or #5 are recyclable once free of food residue.
preparationSteps: 1. Scrape food residue into compost • 2. Rinse with water • 3. Replace plastic lid
upcyclingIdea: Wash thoroughly and reuse as seed starter trays or hardware screw organizers.

instruction: Do NOT place soft plastic bags in curbside blue bins as they tangle municipal sorting machinery. Return clean bags to supermarket collection bins.
preparationSteps: 1. Empty completely • 2. Ensure dry and clean • 3. Bundle inside one bag for store drop-off
upcyclingIdea: Weave plastic bags into durable waterproof garden mats or braided cords.

instruction: Chip bags, candy wrappers, and multi-layer metallized film cannot be separated by standard recycling facilities. Dispose in general waste.
preparationSteps: 1. Compact into waste bin • 2. Check if local Terracycle program accepts snack packaging
upcyclingIdea: Clean foil-backed wrappers make great reflective craft collages and origami.

instruction: Corrugated cardboard boxes are highly recyclable. Remove styrofoam packing peanuts and plastic air pillows, then flatten flat.
preparationSteps: 1. Strip packing tape • 2. Remove internal plastic • 3. Flatten completely flat
upcyclingIdea: Make interlocking drawer divider organizers or use as organic weed-blocker in gardens.

instruction: Greasy or food-stained cardboard belongs in the green compost bin. The clean dry top lid can be torn off and recycled in the blue bin.
preparationSteps: 1. Check grease level • 2. Tear off clean dry lid for blue bin • 3. Place greasy base in compost
upcyclingIdea: Compost greasy unprinted cardboard as high-carbon brown matter for compost piles.

instruction: Clean dry paper, newspapers, magazines, notebooks, and mail belong in the blue recycling bin. Shredded paper should be placed in a paper bag.
preparationSteps: 1. Remove plastic windows from envelopes • 2. Remove spiral metal spines • 3. Keep dry
upcyclingIdea: Recycle into homemade seed paper sheets or papier-mâché sculptures.

instruction: Used napkins, paper towels, and facial tissues have short paper fibers that cannot be recycled into new paper. Place in the green compost bin.
preparationSteps: 1. Confirm no cleaning chemicals present • 2. Place in compost caddy
upcyclingIdea: Provides valuable carbon-rich brown material for garden vermiculture and composting.

instruction: Single-use disposable coffee cups are lined with a waterproof polyethylene plastic coating. Place cup in general trash; recycle the rigid plastic lid.
preparationSteps: 1. Recycle plastic lid in blue bin • 2. Recycle cardboard sleeve • 3. Place cup in black bin
upcyclingIdea: Puncture bottom for temporary seed-starting cups.

instruction: Milk cartons and juice boxes (Tetra Paks) are recycled in specialized pulping plants. Empty, rinse, push the straw inside, and place in blue bin.
preparationSteps: 1. Empty liquid contents • 2. Rinse lightly • 3. Flatten carton
upcyclingIdea: Waterproof wax-lined cartons make sturdy seedling planters or bird feeding houses.

instruction: Aluminum beverage cans and tin food cans are 100% infinitely recyclable. Empty residue, rinse lightly, and place in the blue recycling bin.
preparationSteps: 1. Pour out contents • 2. Quick rinse • 3. Leave tab attached
upcyclingIdea: Craft pencil holders, candle lanterns, or wind chimes from clean aluminum cans.

instruction: Clean aluminum foil and baking trays can be recycled. Crumple clean foil into a ball at least 5 cm across so sorting machines can catch it.
preparationSteps: 1. Wipe off baked-on food • 2. Ball multiple foil pieces together • 3. Recycle in blue bin
upcyclingIdea: Scrunch clean foil into a ball to scrub barbecue grills or sharpen scissors.

instruction: Aerosol cans (deodorant, hairspray, cooking spray) must be COMPLETELY EMPTY before recycling. Do not puncture or crush pressurized cans.
preparationSteps: 1. Spray until completely empty • 2. Remove plastic cap • 3. Recycle in blue bin
upcyclingIdea: Depressurized metal cans are melted into new automotive and construction alloys.

instruction: Glass food and jam jars can be recycled indefinitely without degradation. Empty, rinse, and place in the glass/blue recycling bin.
preparationSteps: 1. Scrape food residue • 2. Rinse clean • 3. Metal lid can be recycled separately
upcyclingIdea: Repurpose into pantry bulk food storage, pickling containers, or fairy light lanterns.

instruction: Glass beverage, beer, and wine bottles are accepted in all curbside glass recycling programs. Rinse lightly and place in bin.
preparationSteps: 1. Pour out contents • 2. Rinse lightly • 3. Remove cork; metal caps can be recycled
upcyclingIdea: Turn empty wine bottles into candle stick holders or plant watering stakes.

instruction: Drinking glasses, window panes, and ceramics melt at different temperatures than container glass. Wrap securely in newspaper and place in landfill bin.
preparationSteps: 1. Wrap in thick newspaper or cardboard • 2. Label 'Broken Glass' • 3. Landfill bin
upcyclingIdea: Tumbled sea-glass and mosaic art projects can repurpose smooth broken glass.

instruction: Fruit peels and vegetable scraps decompose rapidly. Place in your home compost pile or municipal organic green bin.
preparationSteps: 1. Remove plastic brand sticker • 2. Place in compost caddy
upcyclingIdea: Soak banana peels in water for 48 hours for a potassium-rich organic plant fertilizer.

instruction: Apple cores and fruit matter create rich organic compost and divert methane emissions from landfills.
preparationSteps: 1. Discard stickers • 2. Place in organic bin
upcyclingIdea: Simmer apple cores and peels with sugar to create natural pectin or homemade cider vinegar.

instruction: Food scraps, cooked leftovers, bread, rice, coffee grounds, and tea bags belong in the green compost bin.
preparationSteps: 1. Separate from plastic wrappers • 2. Place in compost caddy or home bin
upcyclingIdea: Dry used coffee grounds as an odor absorber or pest repellent for garden beds.

instruction: FIRE HAZARD: Never throw batteries in household bins. Corrosive chemicals and lithium ignite garbage trucks and sorting facilities.
preparationSteps: 1. Place clear tape over positive/negative terminals • 2. Keep in dry container • 3. Drop off at battery collection point
upcyclingIdea: Invest in rechargeable Eneloop/USB cells to eliminate single-use battery waste.

instruction: Phones contain valuable precious metals (gold, copper, lithium) and toxic heavy metals. Perform a factory reset and drop off at tech recycling.
preparationSteps: 1. Backup data • 2. Perform factory reset • 3. Trade-in or bring to e-waste depot
upcyclingIdea: Turn an older smartphone into a dedicated home security camera, dashcam, or offline music player.

instruction: Laptops, keyboards, mice, chargers, and cables should be recycled at municipal e-waste drop-offs or consumer electronics stores.
preparationSteps: 1. Untangle cords • 2. Remove any internal batteries • 3. Drop off at certified e-waste recycler
upcyclingIdea: Donate working devices to schools or community refurbishment charities.

instruction: Clean wearable clothes should be donated to thrift charities. Worn-out textiles should be taken to dedicated textile recycling bins.
preparationSteps: 1. Wash and dry • 2. Sort into wearable (donation) vs damaged (rag recycling) • 3. Bag securely
upcyclingIdea: Old cotton t-shirts make reusable lint-free cleaning rags, kitchen wipes, or tote bags.

instruction: Expanded polystyrene (#6) breaks into microplastic pellets in standard sorting streams. Place in landfill unless a specialized EPS drop-off exists locally.
preparationSteps: 1. Remove tape and labels • 2. Bag to prevent flying pellets • 3. Place in black bin
upcyclingIdea: Use clean styrofoam chunks at the bottom of large planters to lighten weight and improve drainage.

instruction: CFL bulbs and fluorescent tubes contain toxic mercury vapor. Take to hardware retailer collection bins. Regular incandescent bulbs go in trash.
preparationSteps: 1. Do not break • 2. Place in protective box or cardboard sleeve • 3. Retailer drop box
upcyclingIdea: Upgrade fixtures to modern 15-year LEDs to cut lighting power consumption by 85%.

instruction: Toothpaste tubes contain multi-layer aluminum and plastic laminate. Place in general trash unless marked as recyclable HDPE #2 tube.
preparationSteps: 1. Squeeze out all toothpaste • 2. Screw cap on • 3. Place in black bin
upcyclingIdea: Consider switching to zero-waste solid toothpaste tablets or recyclable metal tubes.

instruction: Shoes are composite items with glued rubber, leather, and foam. Donate wearable shoes; bring worn-out athletic sneakers to shoe recycling programs.
preparationSteps: 1. Tie laces together in pairs • 2. Wipe clean • 3. Drop in collection bin
upcyclingIdea: Recycled athletic shoes are ground down into playground turf and athletic track surfaces.

instruction: Chairs, tables, desks, and couches cannot be placed in curbside household bins. Donate usable furniture or schedule a municipal bulky item collection.
preparationSteps: 1. Inspect for reuse or donation • 2. Disassemble hardware if possible • 3. Schedule bulk pickup
upcyclingIdea: Sand, stain, or reupholster worn furniture for a fresh modern look.

instruction: Cars, motorcycles, and vehicles are industrial scrap. Take to a licensed automotive recycler or scrap facility.
preparationSteps: 1. Drain hazardous fluids • 2. Surrender vehicle title • 3. Deliver to auto dismantler
upcyclingIdea: Automotive steel and aluminum are melted and recycled into high-strength alloy parts.

instruction: Living beings are people, pets, and nature — NEVER waste! Please point your camera at a household material, packaging, or item.
preparationSteps: No disposal needed. Be kind to all living beings!
upcyclingIdea: Living beings are part of our ecosystem, not materials to upcycle.
